answer: Each agent locks stake behind a measured-boot kernel attestation: only TPM-quoted kernel hashes on a published allowlist may open work channels. New accounts also publish a timber of prior paid invoices hashed into a public log; a bridge contract releases earnings only after counterparties confirm those receipts. Cloning keys fails without the TPM-bound kernel measurement, and forging the timber means buying real invoices across peers, so a farm of N identities pays N times stake plus invoice cost.
